solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What miserable shed is after forge explodes

indicators.note: something that explodes is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grim picture of a blacksmith's forge blowing up and the sorry state of the shed beside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a noun (the building beside the forge) but is the past tense of a verb: what a miserable person sheds. 'explodes' rearranges ISAFTERFORGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhappy people weep, so the drops they let fall are the outward sign of sorrow.

clue.text: Issues seem unlikely to peserve energy

indicators.note: to preserve something is to keep it safe within, so one piece holds the other; printed with a typo for preserve
an unlikely arrangement suggests the letters are in an improbable order and must be rearranged

parts.note: the erg is a small unit of energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone doubts that certain matters will keep their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlikely' turns SEEM into EMES, which 'to peserve' (a typo for 'preserve') wraps round the unit. 'Issues' is a verb meaning comes out, not a noun meaning problems.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue from somewhere is to come out of it, the verb sense of appearing.

clue.text: I rise to accept great awards

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue rising means being read from bottom to top, so this word is turned round

parts.note: in a crossword the setter often refers to themself as I
OS is the abbreviation for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Someone stands up to receive a big prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter, SETTER; 'rise' turns it to RETTES, which takes in OS. Strictly 'rise' needs 'I must rise' to work grammatically, as the blog notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosettes of ribbon are given as prizes at shows and competitions, so they are a kind of award.

clue.text: See 13 across
What life and people buying you bedding may do

definitions.meaning: life may depress you, making you feel low

definitions.text: people buying you bedding may do
definitions.meaning: people buying you a quilt may supply you with soft feathers for it

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: life may make you feel low, and people may buy you a soft feather filling (down) for your bedding.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to depress someone, and its literal reading means obtaining feathers for someone.

clue.text: Fancies bride a serious amount

indicators.note: an amount is a portion of something, so a portion of these words is taken out as the answer

explanation.surface: Someone's whims run to a bride costing a great deal of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amount' signals a run of letters taken from 'bride a serious'. Some solvers find it a weak signal for this.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancies, as a noun, are notions or thoughts that come into the mind.

clue.text: See 13 across
Today, son of refuse collector would have reached Eighty Nine, Dog Lane on round

definitions.text: Today, son of refuse collector would have reached Eighty

indicators.note: going round suggests turning things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A birthday tribute to a dustman's son, with what looks like an address on a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' rearranges NINEDOGLANEON. The skiffle singer was born on 29 April 1931 and would have been 80 on the day this puzzle appeared; he sang 'My Old Man's a Dustman', which is where the refuse collector comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: The British skiffle star was born on 29 April 1931 and had a hit about a dustman father.

clue.text: Problem of sermon, I see, was ability to induce boredom

indicators.note: a problem with these words means they are a puzzle to be worked out by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A churchgoer notes that the trouble with the sermon was how dull it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem of' rearranges SERMONISEEWAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome sends you to sleep, so the quality of being tedious is the power to bore.

clue.text: Command Archbishop's position

definitions.meaning: to command something is to be in charge of it and supervise it
an archbishop sits above the dioceses of his province, so he is placed over each see

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words: an archbishop's place is above a see, the diocese of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise or be in charge of work is to command it, and an archbishop stands above each see.

clue.text: Elegant, awkward, not large, with energy of seven difficult years

indicators.note: an awkward arrangement is a clumsy one, so these letters are rearranged
not having something means it is removed from the word

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An adolescent who is elegant but awkward, not big, and full of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes L out, leaving EEGANT, which 'awkward' rearranges to TEENAG. Teenage years run from thirteen to nineteen, seven of them.
explanation.definitionFit: The years from thirteen to nineteen are seven in number and famously trying for families.

clue.text: See 13
Today, smug Prince enthrones his out-of-this-world Vogue lover — beg composition by 8

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the preceding words are rearranged to form it

parts.note: the setter's fodder has one R too many; dropping the R of lover makes the letters fit

explanation.surface: Gossip about a royal wedding day: a smug prince crowning his glamorous fashion-magazine sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges all the words from 'Today' to 'beg', but they contain one R too many, a setter's slip. The 1924 song was a skiffle hit for 8-down, who would have turned 80 on the royal wedding day.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelty song was a 1959 hit recording by the skiffle singer of 8-down.

clue.text: Female these days wearing clothing cut short near bottom

indicators.note: a thing being worn sits inside the clothing, so one piece goes inside the other
a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A woman in modern trimmed clothes is close to her lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the last letter, leaving ATTIR, and 'wearing' puts the female and the era inside. The nadir is the lowest point, hence near the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, so being there is being close to rock bottom.

clue.text: Season when everything starts to flower before spring, maybe

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden flower
a spring tide is one kind of tide, the high tide at new and full moon

explanation.surface: A description of the time of year when plants come into bloom ahead of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is the spring tide, hence 'maybe' for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season following Easter Sunday is a period of the year, so it is a season.

clue.text: Flower discovered by Sir Isaac Newton

indicators.note: something discovered is found, here found lying inside these words

explanation.surface: A botanical find credited to the great physicist.
explanation.walkthrough: Newton, famous for optics, is a nice distraction since the word is also part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded flag is a garden plant with showy blooms.

clue.text: Not remotely sophisticated individual

parts.note: in means fashionable, the thing sophisticated people follow

explanation.surface: A description of a classy individual who is very far from being so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not remotely' looks like 'not at all' but means face to face, not at a distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something physically present rather than at a distance is the opposite of doing it remotely.

clue.text: Start of Royal Ballet School's balls

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, taken here from four words in turn

explanation.surface: The first dances given by the Royal Ballet School.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' takes the first letter of each of 'of Royal Ballet School's'. 'balls' looks like dances but means spheres.
explanation.definitionFit: Spheres or globes are round balls, like the orb in the royal regalia.

clue.text: See 13 across
See 13
Divine right knight removed from turbulent older king

indicators.note: turbulent means disordered and churning, so these letters are rearranged
removed from means taken out of the following words

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A turbulent old monarch who rules by divine right, with a knight driven away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes R and N out of OLDERKING, leaving OLDEKIG, which 'turbulent' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Something divine is like a deity, having the qualities of a god.

clue.text: Rubbish pinned to goal

indicators.note: rubbish is a mess, so these letters are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pins a piece of rubbish to the goalposts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' rearranges PINNEDTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A target or aim is the final point where you mean to finish up.

clue.text: See 13 across
Kate does lengthy perspective

definitions.meaning: the bride's surname, Middleton, has its last two letters as O and N
a view taken along the length of something, with its far tip facing the viewer

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a pun on the bride Kate Middleton, whose surname finishes with those two letters: she 'ends on' them.
explanation.definitionFit: A view of something with its tip pointed toward the observer looks along its length.

clue.text: European sets up short dance

indicators.note: in a down clue setting up means raising, so the letters are read upwards, backwards
a word that is short loses its final letter

parts.note: valse is the French word for a waltz, used in English too

explanation.surface: A continental puts on a brief dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims VALSE to VALS, and 'sets up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav belongs to a group of peoples of eastern and central Europe.

clue.text: Assumed obscure poet appears in supplement

indicators.note: appearing in something means showing up inside it
to obscure something is to blur it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little-known poet turns up in a newspaper supplement under a pen name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscure' rearranges the poet to OPTE, and 'appears in' places it inside. 'Assumed' is a past participle, as in an assumed name.
explanation.definitionFit: To take on a name or cause as your own is to assume it, as one assumes a pen name.

clue.text: See 13
William's loveheart kept away from London

indicators.note: something kept is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Prince William, the groom, belongs to the prince
the heart of the word love is its two middle letters

explanation.surface: Prince William's sweetheart is kept away from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveheart' gives the middle of LOVE, OV, which 'kept' places inside THE PRINCE'S. A loveheart is also a British sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Everywhere in Britain outside the capital is traditionally called by this name.
